title: 26. People pleasing - how to say NO!

sentences.en: This is an iHeart PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个iHeart播客。

sentences.en: Guaranteed human.
sentences.zh: 纯正人类创作。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 今年我对待健康的方式有了很大的不同。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去总是很专注于把效率最大化，做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我才意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我如此迷恋我的WHOOP手环。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information-driven person.
sentences.zh: 真的，大家伙儿，你们知道我是一个非常依赖数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my WHOOP app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day-to-day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开WHOOP应用程序，看看我的睡眠、压力、消耗是如何与我的心情、跑步表现以及日常感觉相关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝对算不上什么精英运动员，但我确实受益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很享受去更多地了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And WHOOP also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions
sentences.zh: WHOOP还为我提供这些可操作的、个性化的见解，让我做事更有意识，这意味着我在日常生活中

sentences.en: day-to-day about what I need rather than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 能根据自己的需求做出更明智的决定，而不是只知道踩着油门，不停地、不停地往前冲。

sentences.en: New members can try WHOOP with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新会员在正式订阅会员之前，可以先通过30天免费试用体验WHOOP。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of WHOOP.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com 斜杠 psychology，即可免费体验一个月的WHOOP。

sentences.en: Some people keep all their old gig tickets.
sentences.zh: 有些人会保留他们所有的旧门票。

sentences.en: It brings back the music.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回音乐。

sentences.en: It brings back the memories, even the smells.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回回忆，甚至是气味。

sentences.en: Other people collect perfume bottles or coffee mugs or overseas banknotes, classic sweaters from the 80s.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则收集香水瓶、咖啡杯、海外纸币，或是80年代的经典毛衣。

sentences.en: Collection is deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 收藏是一件极其私人的事情。

sentences.en: It says who we are, but it also says where we've come from.
sentences.zh: 它诉说着我们是谁，但也诉说着我们从哪里来。

sentences.en: In the new podcast, Charmed with Sam Todd, Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 在由萨姆·托德主持的新播客《Charmed》中，萨姆将带你探索那些构成我们的一部分的回忆、执念和微小珍宝。

sentences.en: Charmed with Sam Todd.
sentences.zh: 对山姆·托德着迷。

sentences.en: Stories want to tell with Pandora.
sentences.zh: Pandora倾情呈献的故事。

sentences.en: Listen to the podcast now on iHeart.
sentences.zh: 现在即可在iHeart上收听该播客。

sentences.en: Hello and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，这是一个探讨我们在二十岁时遇到的一些重大生活改变

sentences.en: and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 与转折，以及这些改变对我们的心理意味着什么的播客。

sentences.en: Hello and welcome back to the podcast, to the show.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到本播客，欢迎来到本节目。

sentences.en: Hope you've been amazing and you're feeling loved and motivated, inspired by your life at the moment.
sentences.zh: 希望你们一直都过得很棒，并且在此时此刻感受到生活的爱意、动力和灵感。

sentences.en: I'm feeling great.
sentences.zh: 我感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: But if not, well, maybe this episode can explain just an aspect of why that may not be the case.
sentences.zh: 但如果不是这样，嗯，也许本期节目能解释这种状况背后的一部分原因。

sentences.en: I'm guessing if you're listening to this, if you clicked on this, then this topic probably resonates for you in many ways.
sentences.zh: 我猜如果你正在听这个节目，如果你点开了它，那么这个话题在很多方面一定能引起你的共鸣。

sentences.en: So let's not waste any more valuable time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们别再浪费宝贵的时间了。

sentences.en: I have a lot to discuss today, but I don't want to make another
sentences.zh: 我今天有很多话要聊，但我不想再录一期像几周前那样

sentences.en: 50-minute episode like I did a couple weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 长达50分钟的节目了。

sentences.en: I've realized recently, sorry, here I go rambling, not even a minute in.
sentences.zh: 我最近意识到——抱歉，我又开始废话了，甚至还不到一分钟呢。

sentences.en: But I realized that listening to one of my episodes normally takes the same amount of time for me as it does to get to my local beach, between 22 to 30 minutes.
sentences.zh: 但我意识到，听我的一期节目通常花掉我的时间和去我家附近的海滩差不多，大概在22到30分钟之间。

sentences.en: Hence why I'm trying to keep them more bite-sized.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我试图让节目更加精简干练。

sentences.en: How sweet.
sentences.zh: 多贴心啊。

sentences.en: Yes, I do listen to my own podcast in the car.
sentences.zh: 没错，我确实会在车里听我自己的播客。

sentences.en: And yes, it's strictly for professional purposes and reasons because I don't always listen over them when I press publish because I am lazy.
sentences.zh: 而且没错，这完全是出于职业目的和原因，因为我点击发布的时候并不总是会把它们从头到尾听一遍，因为我很懒。

sentences.en: So I have to do my due diligence later on.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须在事后补上我的尽职调查。

sentences.en: Anyhow, today we're talking about people-pleasing, what it is, how to break the cycle, the trouble it gets us into,
sentences.zh: 言归正传，今天我们要聊的是讨好型人格，它是什么，如何打破这种循环，它给我们带来的麻烦，

sentences.en: and why you're kind of getting in your own way by refusing to say no.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么你因为拒绝说“不”而实际上在给自己制造障碍。

sentences.en: This episode was inspired by many conversations with one of my bestest of friends, Erin, and one of my most loyal listeners.
sentences.zh: 本期节目的灵感来自于我和我最好的朋友之一——艾琳（Erin）的多次聊天，她也是我最忠实的听众之一。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, I miss her.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪，我太想她了。

sentences.en: I miss her so much, but shout out if you're listening, which you probably are.
sentences.zh: 我太想念她了，如果你在听的话——你可能正在听——给你打个招呼。

sentences.en: I'll see you soon.
sentences.zh: 我们很快就会见面。

sentences.en: But we chat about this a lot because I think it's a behavioral pattern we both fall into quite frequently.
sentences.zh: 但我们经常聊起这个，因为我认为这是我们俩都经常陷入的一种行为模式。

sentences.en: And it came up recently because she was up in Sydney for my birthday.
sentences.zh: 这个话题最近之所以被提起，是因为她来悉尼给我过生日。

sentences.en: And while she was here, I was talking about how I was like almost anxious because if I didn't enjoy myself, even if I didn't enjoy myself, sorry,
sentences.zh: 在她来这儿的时候，我提到我当时甚至有点焦虑，因为如果我玩得不够开心——哪怕我其实玩得不开心，抱歉——

sentences.en: I wanted everyone else to be having a really good time.
sentences.zh: 我也希望其他所有人都能玩得非常开心。

sentences.en: I wanted them to be happy.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们能快乐。

sentences.en: And she said, Gemma, that's people-pleasing to a T.
sentences.zh: 她就说：“杰玛，这绝对是标准的讨好型人格。”

sentences.en: And here we are doing an episode on it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就来到了这里，专门做了一期关于这个话题的节目。

sentences.en: Strap in and get ready to learn.
sentences.zh: 系好安全带，准备好学习吧。

sentences.en: The idea of people-pleasing has had a pretty steady rise in pop culture and psychology pop culture, I guess, these last few years.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几年里，“讨好型人格”这个概念在流行文化以及心理学流行文化中可以说是稳步走红。

sentences.en: I think probably due to the increasingly individual nature, the trend or kind of perspective of psychology in its applications to our lives
sentences.zh: 我想这可能是由于心理学在我们生活中的应用越来越趋于个人主义的性质、趋势或某种视角，

sentences.en: and the focus on self-growth and self-awareness.
sentences.zh: 以及对自我成长和自我觉察的关注。

sentences.en: And the idea is also quite a recent one, the idea of people-pleasing.
sentences.zh: 而且“讨好型人格”这个概念其实也相当新颖。

sentences.en: Obviously, the behavior has been around for a while.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这种行为存在已久。

sentences.en: We just haven't always, I guess, had a name for it.
sentences.zh: 只是我们以前不总是能，或者说，为它找到一个名字。

sentences.en: But there have even been like poems written about it.
sentences.zh: 但甚至还有人写过关于它的诗。

sentences.en: So one is pretty dramatic.
sentences.zh: 其中有一首非常戏剧化。

sentences.en: I found it when I was researching this episode and I thought it was quite funny.
sentences.zh: 我是在为这期节目做研究时发现它的，我觉得挺搞笑的。

sentences.en: Wait, let me read a line.
sentences.zh: 等等，让我读一句。

sentences.en: Where is it?
sentences.zh: 在哪儿呢？

sentences.en: I always say yes, can never say no, swallow all hurt, let no feelings show.
sentences.zh: 我总是说“好”，从不说“不”，吞下所有委屈，不让情绪表露。

sentences.en: He insulted me badly, called me the son of a bore.
sentences.zh: 他狠狠地侮辱我，骂我是个讨厌鬼的儿子。

sentences.en: I just rolled over saying, kick me, kick me more.
sentences.zh: 我只是打了个滚说：“来吧，狠狠地踢我吧。”

sentences.en: Some very dramatic lines from that poet, Alan Bruce Thompson.
sentences.zh: 来自诗人艾伦·布鲁斯·汤普森（Alan Bruce Thompson）的一些非常戏剧化的诗句。

sentences.en: Thank you for your inspiring, if not depressing, lyric, Alan.
sentences.zh: 艾伦，谢谢你的这首就算说不上沮丧、也算得上激励的抒情诗。

sentences.en: But I don't know why I said that.
sentences.zh: 不过我不知道我为什么要说这个。

sentences.en: But I think it's just interesting.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这挺有意思的。

sentences.en: I don't know why I felt the need to cite this poem that I had in my research.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么我觉得有必要引用这首我在资料里看到的诗。

sentences.en: But I think it's just an indicator of how long this behavior has kind of been part of a dialogue around our interactions with other people.
sentences.zh: 但我想这只是一个标志，表明这种行为作为我们与他人互动对话的一部分已经存在了多久。

sentences.en: And people-pleasing has become such a popular term, though, that it has, wait for it, its own WebMD page.
sentences.zh: 不过，“讨好型人格”这个词现在实在太火了，以至于它——你猜怎么着——居然有专属的 WebMD 网页。

sentences.en: Yes, ladies and gentlemen, you know the site you go to check if your headache may be, I don't know, cancer?
sentences.zh: 没错，各位女士先生，你们都知道那个用来查你的头痛是不是——我不知道——癌症的网站？

sentences.en: Well, that site can now diagnose you with people-pleasing.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那个网站现在能给你诊断出讨好型人格了。

sentences.en: It's also inspired numerous psychology books such as The Disease to Please and When It's Never
sentences.zh: 它还启发了许多心理学书籍，比如《取悦的病态》和《当它从不》

sentences.en: About You, titles that are almost as dramatic as our friend Alan's poem, but you get the giSt.
sentences.zh: 《与你有关》，这些书名和我们朋友艾伦的诗一样富有戏剧性，但你懂我的意思。

sentences.en: People-pleasing is now a pretty common, popular part of daily psychobabble.
sentences.zh: 讨好型人格现在成了日常心理学黑话中一个相当普遍、热门的部分。

sentences.en: So what is people-pleasing?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是讨好型人格呢？

sentences.en: Yes, it does kind of say it all in the name, but let's dig a little deeper as we tend to do in this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，字面意思其实已经说明了一切，但让我们像在这个播客中经常做的那样，再深入探讨一下。

sentences.en: Essentially, people-pleasers are those who cannot maintain clear boundaries with others and do really whatever it takes essentially to make other people happy.
sentences.zh: 本质上，讨好者是指那些无法与他人保持清晰界限，并且基本上不惜一切代价让其他人开心的人。

sentences.en: They're often highly attuned to others and seen as agreeable, helpful, really kind.
sentences.zh: 他们通常对他人高度敏感，被视为随和、乐于助人、真的很善良。

sentences.en: However, people-pleasers may have trouble advocating for themselves, which can lead to a pretty harmful pattern of self-sacrifice and self-neglect.
sentences.zh: 然而，讨好者可能很难为自己发声，这可能会导致一种相当有害的自我牺牲和自我忽视的模式。

sentences.en: I think whilst it's generally seen as a positive attribute to want to help others and act pro-socially
sentences.zh: 我认为，虽然想要帮助他人并以亲社会的方式行事

sentences.en: and in a way that kind of aligns with this entrenched altruistic norm, when we begin to
sentences.zh: 且这种方式在某种程度上符合这种根深蒂固的利他主义规范，通常被视为一种积极的品质，但当我们开始

sentences.en: see ourselves as second to the needs of others, you will inevitably end up depleted and anxious.
sentences.zh: 将自己视为次于他人需求的存在时，你不可避免地会感到精疲力竭和焦虑。

sentences.en: And you also tend to experience disconnect with yourself and become unable to recognize or express what you need from a situation or from others in your lives.
sentences.zh: 而且你往往也会体验到与自我的断连，变得无法识别或表达你从某种情境或生活中的其他人那里需要什么。

sentences.en: Like I've kind of said already, a key element of people-pleasing is that it generally goes beyond simple kindness.
sentences.zh: 就像我刚才已经说过的，讨好型人格的一个关键要素是它通常超越了简单的善良。

sentences.en: It involves, you know, editing or altering words and behaviors for the sake of another person's feelings or reactions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它涉及到为了另一个人的感受或反应而修改或改变言行。

sentences.en: And that was explained by Erica Myers.
sentences.zh: 这是由埃里卡·迈尔斯解释的。

sentences.en: And she's a therapist in the US at the University of Oregon.
sentences.zh: 她是美国俄勒冈大学的一名治疗师。

sentences.en: This is what else she kind of had to say.
sentences.zh: 这就是她想说的其他内容。

sentences.en: You might go out of your way to do things for the people in your life based on what you assume, what you assume they want or need.
sentences.zh: 你可能会根据你假设的、你假设他们想要或需要的东西，竭尽全力为你生活中的人做事。

sentences.en: And you give up your time and energy to get them to like you, to get them to love you more.
sentences.zh: 你放弃时间和精力是为了让他们喜欢你，让他们更爱你。

sentences.en: And Myers says that this is how people-pleasing, it's a bit of a tongue twister, how people-pleasing can cause trouble.
sentences.zh: 迈尔斯说，这就是讨好型人格——这有点拗口——是如何引发问题的。

sentences.en: The urge to please others can be damaging to ourselves and potentially to our relationships when we allow other people's wants to have more importance than our own needs.
sentences.zh: 当我们允许其他人的愿望比我们自己的需求更重要时，取悦他人的冲动可能会对我们自己以及潜在的我们的关系造成损害。

sentences.en: And when we try to anticipate what others want from us without trusting that they can advocate for themselves.
sentences.zh: 当我们试图预测别人对我们的期望，却又不相信他们能够为自己发声时。

sentences.en: It's a pretty well-known rule of thumb that relationships, they should be equal, give and take.
sentences.zh: 这是一个广为人知的经验法则，即关系应该是平等的，有付出就有回报。

sentences.en: I think that's the, I think that the previous overview of people-pleasing, it shouldn't be
sentences.zh: 我认为，呃，前面关于讨好型人格的概述，不应该

sentences.en: taken to mean that you can never offer assistance for others because you might be placing your second.
sentences.zh: 被理解为你就永远不能为他人提供帮助，因为那样你可能会把自己排在第二位。

sentences.en: No, it's all about balance, baby.
sentences.zh: 不，这一切都在于平衡，宝贝。

sentences.en: What I find really interesting with people-pleasing behaviors is how our brain literally hijacks
sentences.zh: 我发现讨好行为中最有趣的是，我们的大脑是如何字面上地劫持了

sentences.en: itself to not only be better at recognizing other people's needs over our own, but happy to do things for others at our own expense.
sentences.zh: 它自己，不仅为了更擅长识别别人的需求而不是我们自己的需求，而且还乐意以牺牲我们自己的利益为代价为别人做事。

sentences.en: It's so counterintuitive and counter to kind of an evolutionary idea of survival.
sentences.zh: 这太违反直觉了，也违背了某种生存的进化理念。

sentences.en: So here are some pretty typical indicators of being a people-pleaser, not just someone who's happy to help a friend, a partner, or, you know, a neighbor out, but a full-blown
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一些成为讨好型人格的典型指标，不仅仅是一个乐于帮助朋友、伴侣或者，你知道，邻居的人，而是一个彻头彻尾的

sentences.en: people-pleaser.
sentences.zh: 讨好者。

sentences.en: So you have a difficult time saying no, you're preoccupied with what others might think of you, which we're going to talk about a lot later on.
sentences.zh: 所以你很难说不，你满脑子都在想着别人可能会怎么看你，我们稍后会详细讨论这一点。

sentences.en: You feel guilty when you have to tell people no.
sentences.zh: 当你不得不对别人说不时，你会感到内疚。

sentences.en: You fear that turning people down will make them think that you are selfish.
sentences.zh: 你担心拒绝别人会让他们觉得你很自私。

sentences.en: You agree to things that you don't like or do things that you don't want to do.
sentences.zh: 你会答应一些自己不喜欢的事情，或者去做一些你根本不想做的事。

sentences.en: This is really common with some of my friends, you know, they sign up for things or they offer to help a friend out and they just really need, you know, some alone time.
sentences.zh: 我有些朋友就经常这样，你知道的，他们答应参加活动，或者主动提出去帮朋友的忙，而他们其实非常需要，你知道的，一点独处的时间。

sentences.en: It's not what they need to go and socialize more.
sentences.zh: 他们需要的并不是去社交更多。

sentences.en: You might struggle with feelings of low self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 你可能正饱受自卑感的困扰。

sentences.en: You want people to like you and you feel that doing things for them will in some ways earn their approval.
sentences.zh: 你渴望别人喜欢你，并且觉得为他们做事在某种程度上能赢得他们的认可。

sentences.en: You're always telling people sorry and you're taking blame for things, even when it isn't your fault.
sentences.zh: 你总是向别人道歉，把责任揽到自己身上，即使那根本不是你的错。

sentences.en: And think about what kind of life that would entail if you're constantly apologizing for things, always in the guilt trap our brains have created or being so preoccupied with what
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果你总是为事情道歉，一直陷在我们的大脑制造的内疚陷阱中，或者过度在意

sentences.en: others think that you can't really ever seem to consider yourself.
sentences.zh: 别人的看法，以至于你似乎永远无法真正去关照自己，那将会是怎样的一种生活。

sentences.en: And it's no surprise that psychologists and researchers have found heaps of known links between people pleasing and disorders like social anxiety, OCD and depression.
sentences.zh: 心理学家和研究人员发现，讨好型人格与社交焦虑、强迫症和抑郁症等疾病之间存在大量已知的关联，这并不令人意外。

sentences.en: So where does this type of behavior come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种行为究竟从何而来呢？

sentences.en: I want to jump into some very interesting links later on, mainly around trauma and gender.
sentences.zh: 我稍后想探讨一些非常有趣的关联，主要围绕创伤和性别。

sentences.en: But before then, let's talk about some of the more typical causes of people pleasing behavior.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，让我们先谈谈讨好型行为的一些更典型的诱因。

sentences.en: So firstly, and we've talked about this in some of the indicators, but poor self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们在一些表现中也讨论过，那就是糟糕的自尊心。

sentences.en: So sometimes people engage in people pleasing behavior because they don't value their own desires and needs.
sentences.zh: 有时人们会有讨好他人的行为，是因为他们不珍视自己的愿望和需求。

sentences.en: Perhaps due to a lack of self-confidence, people pleasers have a need for external validation and they may feel that doing things for others will lead to approval and acceptance.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为缺乏自信，讨好型人格有着对外部认可的需求，他们可能会觉得为别人做事会带来认可和接纳。

sentences.en: People pleasing behavior is not always an expression of goodwill.
sentences.zh: 讨好型行为并不总是善意的表达。

sentences.en: It comes from a longing to feel socially secure.
sentences.zh: 它源于对获得社交安全感的渴望。

sentences.en: And it's a symptom of a generalized fear of abandonment, which usually comes from the relationships we have with our parents or our caregivers and a general sense of self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 它是普遍存在的被抛弃恐惧的一种症状，这种恐惧通常源于我们与父母或照顾者的关系以及整体的自尊感。

sentences.en: So this this other idea in psychology called self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 心理学中还有另一个概念叫做自我效能感。

sentences.en: So self-esteem and self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 也就是自尊心和自我效能感。

sentences.en: Self-efficacy, it refers to an individual's belief in their capacity to execute behaviors necessary to produce specific performance attainments.
sentences.zh: 自我效能感是指个人对自己有能力执行产生特定绩效表现所需行为的信念。

sentences.en: So basically, it kind of reflects your confidence in your ability to exert control over your own motivations, your social environment and the health of your relationship.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，它在某种程度上反映了你对掌控自己动机、社交环境以及人际关系健康状况的能力的自信。

sentences.en: So what's really interesting about self-efficacy is that researchers haven't yet been able to determine the direction of that relationship.
sentences.zh: 关于自我效能感，非常有趣的一点是，研究人员尚未确定这种关系的因果方向。

sentences.en: So whether low or high self-efficacy contributes to people pleasing tendencies more.
sentences.zh: 也就是究竟是低自我效能感还是高自我效能感，对讨好倾向的影响更大。

sentences.en: So on one hand, if you feel like you do have a lot of control over the quality of your
sentences.zh: 一方面，如果你觉得自己对人际关系的质量有很大的控制力

sentences.en: relationships, you may be more likely to engage in people pleasing behaviors because that's one of your tactics for control.
sentences.zh: 你可能更倾向于做出讨好他人的行为，因为那是你掌控局面的策略之一。

sentences.en: But in contrast, feeling like you don't have a lot of control may lead you to overcompensate and try to constantly help others.
sentences.zh: 但相比之下，觉得自己缺乏控制力可能会导致你过度补偿，试图不断地去帮助别人。

sentences.en: If anyone has the answers to that conundrum link between self-efficacy and people pleasing behaviors, please let the psychological community know they'd be very interested.
sentences.zh: 如果有人知道自我效能感与讨好行为之间那个谜题的答案，请告知心理学界，他们会非常感兴趣的。

sentences.en: Perfectionism is another huge, huge determining factor of people pleasing.
sentences.zh: 完美主义是导致讨好型人格的另一个极其重要的决定性因素。

sentences.en: We've talked about this many times before on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们以前在播客里多次讨论过这一点。

sentences.en: It comes up all the time.
sentences.zh: 这总是被提起。

sentences.en: But sometimes people want everything to be just so, including how other people think and feel about them.
sentences.zh: 但有时人们希望一切都恰到好处，包括别人如何看待和感受他们。

sentences.en: Helping others, prioritizing them makes you seem more likable and keeps those people in your life.
sentences.zh: 帮助他人、将他们置于优先地位会让你显得更有亲和力，并将这些人留在你的生活中。

sentences.en: And this gives the perception of a perfect social circle and I guess a perfect vibe.
sentences.zh: 这给人一种完美的社交圈的感觉，我猜也是一种完美的氛围。

sentences.en: And people pleasing and perfectionism, they both come from the ego.
sentences.zh: 讨好行为和完美主义都源于自我（本我/超我中的自我）。

sentences.en: So for those who aren't so familiar with this Freudian idea of the ego, which is different
sentences.zh: 所以，对于那些不太熟悉弗洛伊德关于“自我”这一概念的人来说，这与我们

sentences.en: from our normal conception of the ego as like the arrogant part of ourselves, let me explain.
sentences.zh: 通常把自我理解为我们身上傲慢的那一部分是不同的，让我来解释一下。

sentences.en: So according to Freudian theory, there are three core elements of the human psyche, the id, the ego and the superego.
sentences.zh: 根据弗洛伊德的理论，人类心理有三个核心要素：本我、自我和超我。

sentences.en: So the ego is who we are in the present.
sentences.zh: 所以自我（ego）就是我们在当下所展现的真实的自己。

sentences.en: It's the reality created by the behaviors that we express.
sentences.zh: 它是我们外在行为所创造出的现实。

sentences.en: And the superego and the id, they're kind of like the devil and the angel on your shoulder.
sentences.zh: 而超我和本我，它们有点像你肩膀上的恶魔和天使。

sentences.en: The superego represents pure morality and what society would expect us to do.
sentences.zh: 超我代表了纯粹的道德，以及社会期望我们去做的事。

sentences.en: And the superego is part of the unconscious mind or the psyche that is kind of the voice of conscience and doing what is right.
sentences.zh: 超我是潜意识或心灵的一部分，有点像是良心的声音，指引我们做正确的事。

sentences.en: And there's also the source of self-criticism.
sentences.zh: 它也是自我批判的来源。

sentences.en: In contrast, the sneaky little id is the primitive, instinctive component of your personality.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，鬼鬼祟祟的本我则是你人格中原始、本能的部分。

sentences.en: It's where intrusive thoughts come from.
sentences.zh: intrusive thoughts（侵入性想法）就来源于此。

sentences.en: It contains like our urges, our impulses, and it's where Freud argues our immediate reactions are born.
sentences.zh: 它包含我们的欲望、冲动，弗洛伊德认为我们的即时反应就诞生于此。

sentences.en: So then we arrive at the ego.
sentences.zh: 然后我们来到了自我（ego）。

sentences.en: And the ego is the part of your mind that cares about what others think.
sentences.zh: 自我则是你心中在乎别人看法的那部分。

sentences.en: And it is kind of involved in that balancing act between our pure morals that have been conditioned into us by society and then what we really want to do.
sentences.zh: 它有点像是社会内化给我们的纯粹道德与我们内心真正想做的事情之间的一种平衡机制。

sentences.en: And it's what the ego is what we are aware of when we think about ourselves.
sentences.zh: 当我们思考自己时，自我就是我们所能意识到的那部分。

sentences.en: And it's what we usually try to project towards others.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们通常试图向他人展现的形象。

sentences.en: So this is where people-pleasing behaviors come from.
sentences.zh: 所以，讨好型行为就是这样产生的。

sentences.en: It comes from the part of our brain or our mind that recognizes that we can be perceived by others and wants people to like what they see.
sentences.zh: 它源于我们大脑或心灵中认识到自己会被他人感知、并希望别人喜欢他们所看到的那一部分。

sentences.en: Because of that, because of that recognition of perception, we strive to make others happy.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，出于对这种被感知觉察，我们努力让别人开心。

sentences.en: And when our ego doesn't strike the balance or the correct balance between the superego and
sentences.zh: 而当我们的自我没能在超我和

sentences.en: the id, the side of us that makes it hard to say no and seeks excessive validation, obsessively from others, obsessively from others, yes.
sentences.zh: 本我之间取得平衡或正确的平衡时，我们身上那种难以说“不”、过度且执着地向他人寻求认同的一面就会显露出来，是的，对，就是执着地向他人寻求认同。

sentences.en: Because that's the part that kind of roars its head.
sentences.zh: 因为那是会探出头来的那部分。

sentences.en: And like I said, perfectionism, it's a pretty core aspect linked to people-pleasing.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，完美主义是与讨好型人格密切相关的一个核心方面。

sentences.en: But there is another aspect that's super common amongst those of us who are more concerned with making others happy.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一个方面，在那些更关心让别人开心的人当中非常普遍。

sentences.en: And it's called sociotrophy.
sentences.zh: 它被称为社会依存倾向（sociotrophy）。

sentences.en: Sociotrophy is the tendency to place an inordinate value on our relationships over personal independence.
sentences.zh: 社会依存倾向是指将人际关系看得比个人独立性更重，赋予其不合比例的价值的倾向。

sentences.en: So it's in direct contrast to, I guess, excessive independence or autonomy, which is a concern
sentences.zh: 所以这与那种过度的独立或自主形成了直接对比，后者更关注

sentences.en: with personal achievement and control of your daily life rather than what other people think of you.
sentences.zh: 个人成就和对日常生活的掌控，而不是别人怎么看你。

sentences.en: So people with this trait, sociotrophy, tend to have strong needs for social acceptance,
sentences.zh: 因此，具有这种特质（社会依存倾向）的人，往往对社会接纳有着强烈的需求，

sentences.en: which is what causes them to be overly nurturant towards people who they may not even have a close relationship with or people they might not even like.
sentences.zh: 这导致他们对甚至可能没有密切关系的人，或者他们甚至并不喜欢的人，表现得过于关切和照顾。

sentences.en: And we can really see from kind of a very basic viewpoint why a personality trait such as this would make you more predisposed to people-pleasing and that constant like kind
sentences.zh: 从非常基础的角度，我们确实可以看出，为什么这样的人格特质会让你更容易倾向于讨好他人，并为了迎合他人而不断

sentences.en: of agreeableness for the sake of others.
sentences.zh: 表现出过度的随和。

sentences.en: Whilst not specifically linked to people-pleasing, but something interesting nonetheless is understanding this character trait.
sentences.zh: 虽然它与讨好型人格没有直接联系，但理解这一性格特质依然很有意思。

sentences.en: So people with sociotrophy, they also tend to react really differently than those low on this trait in situations that involve self-control.
sentences.zh: 所以，具有社会依存倾向的人，在涉及自我控制的情境中，其反应往往也与低这种特质的人截然不同。

sentences.en: So in one experiment, they had people who were rated high on the trait of sociotrophy share a meal with another person who was actually an actor.
sentences.zh: 所以在一次实验中，他们让在社会依存倾向特质上得分很高的人与另一个人一起吃饭，而那个人其实是个演员。

sentences.en: And this actor was instructed to either overeat, undereat or not eat at all.
sentences.zh: 这个演员被指示要嘛吃得过多、要嘛吃得过少，要嘛干脆不吃。

sentences.en: Sociotropic individuals in this experiment, they consume more food or they try and match a
sentences.zh: 在这项实验中，具有社会依存倾向的个体当他们相信这样做能让对方（即演员）感到更舒适时，会吃更多的食物，或者试图与

sentences.en: meal with other people-pleasers, eating habits when they believe that doing so will make that person, the actor, feel more comfortable.
sentences.zh: 其他讨好者的饮食习惯保持一致。

sentences.en: And this is often hypothesized as being the result of the individual attempting to achieve social approval and avoid social rejection.
sentences.zh: 这通常被假设为个体试图获得社会认可并避免社会排斥的结果。

sentences.en: The social pressure and dependence can cause a loss of self-control in an individual, especially if they are unaware of their desire for social acceptance.
sentences.zh: 这种社会压力和依赖会导致个体的自控力丧失，特别是当他们没有意识到自己对社会接纳的渴望时。

sentences.en: Now, crucially, sociotrophy has been correlated with feminine or female sex role orientations in many research experiments again and again.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，在许多研究实验中，社会依存倾向被反复证明与女性的性别角色取向相关。

sentences.en: And naturally, the prevalence of people-pleasing behaviors show a similar correlation.
sentences.zh: 自然地，讨好型行为的普遍程度也显示出类似的相关性。

sentences.en: So people-pleasing is more commonly presented in women over men, which I think we could probably have assumed.
sentences.zh: 所以讨好型行为在女性中比在男性中更常见，我想这一点我们大概都能猜到。

sentences.en: One recent study found this behavior to be exhibited in the majority of female participants.
sentences.zh: 最近的一项研究发现，大多数女性参与者都表现出了这种行为。

sentences.en: 59%, whilst only a minority of men, I think around 38%, showed similar tendencies.
sentences.zh: 占 59%，而只有少数男性（我想大概 38% 左右）表现出了类似的倾向。

sentences.en: As a result, women are suffering from greater adverse effects on both their mental and physical health from these behaviors.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，女性正因为这些行为而在身心健康方面遭受更大的负面影响。

sentences.en: The pressure that women feel to be people-pleasers is very real, and it comes from a lot of historical norms around female behavior and their role in society.
sentences.zh: 女性感受到的做讨好者的压力是真实存在的，它源于围绕女性行为及其社会角色的许多历史规范。

sentences.en: Women are conditioned really early to be caregivers and more generous with their time and energy because of their, you know, expectant future role as mothers.
sentences.zh: 由于她们未来作为母亲的预期角色，女性在很小的时候就被社会化为照顾者，并在时间和精力上表现得更加慷慨。

sentences.en: Even if you don't have children, you see how other women in society act and the amount of sacrifices they're asked to make compared to their male counterparts.
sentences.zh: 即使你没有孩子，你也能看到社会上的其他女性如何行事，以及与男性相比，她们被要求做出多少牺牲。

sentences.en: And a lot of these sacrifices are tied to people-pleasing behaviors.
sentences.zh: 而其中许多牺牲都与讨好型行为息息相关。

sentences.en: This is entirely anecdotal, but a lot of my female friends, they struggle saying no.
sentences.zh: 这完全是基于个人经验，但我的很多女性朋友都很难开口说不。

sentences.en: They struggle establishing boundaries at work with partners and their friends, never having free time because they always have things to do with or for other people.
sentences.zh: 她们很难在工作、伴侣和朋友之间建立界限，永远没有空闲时间，因为她们总有做不完的、和别人相关或是为别人做的事情。

sentences.en: And I'm not saying it's a purely gendered thing, but the research doesn't lie.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这是一个纯粹由性别决定的问题，但研究不会说谎。

sentences.en: You know, it's a man's world.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是男人的世界。

sentences.en: Women are just holding it up without people-pleasing behaviors.
sentences.zh: 而女性只是靠着讨好行为在支撑着它。

sentences.en: People-pleasing behaviors, as we've kind of mentioned, they often lead to people taking
sentences.zh: 正如我们刚才提到的，讨好型行为往往会导致别人利用你，

sentences.en: advantage of you, which is why our 20s are such a formative year for setting those boundaries and putting ourselves firSt.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们的二十多岁是为自己设定界限并把自我放在首位的决定性几年。

sentences.en: Some people are really good, specifically sociopaths and narcissists.
sentences.zh: 有些人真的很擅长这一点，特别是反社会人格者和自恋者。

sentences.en: They're really good at recognizing and taking advantage of people who display people-pleasing tendencies.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长识别和利用那些表现出讨好倾向的人。

sentences.en: They may not be able to name their behavior, but they do know that you'll agree to whatever they ask, so they'll keep on asking, and you keep saying yes because you want to keep
sentences.zh: 他们可能说不出这种行为的名称，但他们知道你对他们的任何要求都会满口答应，所以他们会一直提要求，而你也会一直答应，因为你想让他们

sentences.en: them happy.
sentences.zh: 保持开心。

sentences.en: And this can put you at higher risk of, you know, manipulation or mental or emotional abuse, even financial problems if people ask you for, you know, monetary assistance.
sentences.zh: 这会让你面临更高的风险，比如遭受操纵、精神或情感虐待，如果有人向你寻求金钱援助，甚至还会引发财务问题。

sentences.en: We've talked about this a bit as well, but it can also be a real challenge to establishing healthy long-term relationships.
sentences.zh: 我们之前也讨论过这一点，但建立健康的长期关系也可能是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: Healthy, strong, especially romantic relationships, they're balanced and they involve give and take.
sentences.zh: 健康、牢固的恋爱关系尤甚，它们是平衡的，且包含着付出与回报。

sentences.en: You do nice things for your loved ones and they do the same for you.
sentences.zh: 你为所爱的人做美好的事，他们也会为你做同样的事。

sentences.en: You probably won't have very fulfilling romantic relationships when you feel like people will only like you if you do nice, excessive things for them.
sentences.zh: 当你觉得别人只有在你为他们做过度且美好的事情时才会喜欢你时，你可能不会拥有非常满足的恋爱关系。

sentences.en: Affection is not a commodity.
sentences.zh: 感情不是一件商品。

sentences.en: When all you do is give to others to present yourself as the person you think they want, you're not showing up in the relationship as yourself.
sentences.zh: 当你所做的一切只是为了迎合他人，把自己表现为他们所期望的那个人时，你并没有以真实的自我出现在这段关系中。

sentences.en: And it's difficult to maintain, much less feel satisfied with when you aren't actually present in your relationship.
sentences.zh: 当你并未真正投入到你的关系中时，维系它本就很艰难，更不用说从中感到满足了。

sentences.en: Also, I'm super, super sorry if you've had to learn this the hard way, but giving everything
sentences.zh: 另外，如果你不得不以惨痛的代价才明白这一点，我真的、真的感到抱歉，那就是把一切都

sentences.en: to other people, especially a partner or someone you love, thinking it will make them love you.
sentences.zh: 给别人，尤其是伴侣或你爱的人，以为这样就能让他们爱你。

sentences.en: Doing things for them, going out of your way to constantly serve them, teaching them things,
sentences.zh: 为他们做这做那，竭尽全力不断服务他们、教他们东西、

sentences.en: buying them things, letting them walk all over you will never convince them to love you more.
sentences.zh: 给他们买东西、任由他们践踏你的尊严，永远不会让他们更爱你。

sentences.en: And I know that can be where some of these people-pleasing behaviors in romantic relationships can come
sentences.zh: 我知道，恋爱关系中某些讨好行为可能就源于此，因为你觉得如果你为他们的幸福付出更多、做出更多牺牲，

sentences.en: from because you think that if you give more and sacrifice more for their happiness, you'll become someone they can't live without.
sentences.zh: 你就会成为他们生活中不可或缺的人。

sentences.en: They'll turn around, they'll recognize how amazing you are and it's just never going to be the case.
sentences.zh: 他们会回心转意，意识到你有多么了不起，但事实证明这永远不会发生。

sentences.en: I've learned this time and time again.
sentences.zh: 我一次又一次地吸取了这样的教训。

sentences.en: And it never changes.
sentences.zh: 而且情况从来没有变过。

sentences.en: Either they don't recognize it or they just assume that you like doing it, I guess.
sentences.zh: 要么他们认不出来，要么他们只是觉得你喜欢这么做，我猜。

sentences.en: None of this is looking particularly pretty, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，这些看起来都不怎么好看。

sentences.en: So how do we change it and get out of our own way with these people-pleasing tendencies?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该如何改变这种状况，不再让这些讨好他人的倾向阻碍自己呢？

sentences.en: Firstly, show kindness when you mean it.
sentences.zh: 首先，在发自内心地想要善良时表现出善良。

sentences.en: It's perfectly fine and even a really good thing for your mental health to practice kindness.
sentences.zh: 练习善良是完全可以的，甚至对你的心理健康大有裨益。

sentences.en: But kindness, it doesn't come from a desire to earn approval and it generally doesn't involve any motive beyond wanting to make things better for someone else.
sentences.zh: 但善良并非源于获得认可的渴望，通常除了想让别人的处境变得更好之外，它不包含任何其他动机。

sentences.en: Before you offer, you know, words of affirmation or help, consider your intentions and how that act will make you feel.
sentences.zh: 在你提供肯定的话语或帮助之前，先想想你的意图，以及这种行为会给你带来什么感受。

sentences.en: Does the opportunity to help someone else bring you joy or do you think it's going to make you resentful or you're going to feel unappreciated?
sentences.zh: 帮助别人的机会能给你带来快乐，还是你觉得这会让你心生怨恨，或者让你觉得自己不被赏识？

sentences.en: Practice putting yourself firSt.
sentences.zh: 练习把你自己放在首位。

sentences.en: You need energy and emotional resources to help others.
sentences.zh: 你需要精力和情感资源来帮助他人。

sentences.en: And if you don't take care of yourself, you won't be able or capable of doing anything for anyone else in the future.
sentences.zh: 如果你不照顾好自己，将来你将无法或没有能力为任何人做任何事。

sentences.en: Putting your needs first isn't selfish.
sentences.zh: 把你的需求放在第一位并不是自私。

sentences.en: It's actually quite healthy.
sentences.zh: 这其实相当健康。

sentences.en: You know, it's okay to be a giving, caring person, but it's also important to honor and tend to our own needs.
sentences.zh: 要知道，做一个乐于助人、充满关爱的人是没有问题的，但尊重并照顾好我们自己的需求同样重要。

sentences.en: Keep in mind that needs can involve things like offering your opinion in a work meeting, getting comfortable with your emotions and feelings and asking for what you need in your
sentences.zh: 请记住，需求可能包括诸如在工作会议上表达你的意见、习惯并接纳你的情绪和感受，以及在

sentences.en: relationship.
sentences.zh: 恋爱关系中说出你的需求。

sentences.en: That can sometimes do more good than bad.
sentences.zh: 这有时往往利大于弊。

sentences.en: Speaking up for yourself and not just more good for yourself, but more good for those around you if they know where you stand.
sentences.zh: 为自己发声不仅仅是对你自己更好，如果他们知道你的立场，对你周围的人也更好。

sentences.en: We've said it again and again, but learn to set boundaries.
sentences.zh: 我们已经说过很多次了，但要学会设定界限。

sentences.en: So according to this psychologist Myers, developing healthy boundaries is a pretty important step,
sentences.zh: 因此，根据这位心理学家迈尔斯的说法，培养健康的界限是一个相当重要的步骤，

sentences.en: not just in overcoming people-pleasing behaviors, but for setting up any kind of healthy long-term relationship.
sentences.zh: 不仅有助于克服讨好型行为，还能为建立任何健康的长期关系打下基础。

sentences.en: The next time someone asks for help or you're tempted to intervene, consider three things.
sentences.zh: 下次有人请求帮助或者你很想插手时，考虑以下三件事。

sentences.en: How do you feel about the action?
sentences.zh: 你对这个行为有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Is it something you want to do or are you dreading it?
sentences.zh: 这是你想做的事，还是你很畏惧？

sentences.en: You can always just say no.
sentences.zh: 你随时都可以拒绝。

sentences.en: You can always back out.
sentences.zh: 你随时都可以退出。

sentences.en: You don't owe your time or your energy to anyone but yourself.
sentences.zh: 你的时间和精力只属于你自己，不欠任何人。

sentences.en: Think about whether you have time to see to your own needs firSt.
sentences.zh: 想想你是否有时间先照顾好自己的需求。

sentences.en: Will you have to sacrifice your own time or a necessary chore or something you're looking forward to, to helping this other person?
sentences.zh: 为了帮助这个人，你是否不得不牺牲自己的时间、必要的家务或是你所期待的事情？

sentences.en: And how will helping make you feel?
sentences.zh: 并且帮忙会让你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Will it make you feel happy or will it make you feel resentful?
sentences.zh: 这会让你感到快乐，还是会让你感到怨恨？

sentences.en: Finally, wait until you are asked for help.
sentences.zh: 最后，等到别人向你求助时再行动。

sentences.en: No matter what the problem is, you know, if you're a people pleaser, you're always ready with a solution.
sentences.zh: 无论问题是什么，你知道的，如果你是一个老好人，你总是随时准备好解决方案。

sentences.en: You volunteer for things of work, jump in with suggestions when a friend, you know, mentions any kind of problem, offer to help them out.
sentences.zh: 你会主动承担工作上的事情，当朋友提到什么问题时，你会立刻跳出来提建议，主动提出帮忙。

sentences.en: Next time, challenge yourself to wait until someone explicitly asks you for help.
sentences.zh: 下一次，挑战自己，等到别人明确向你求助时再行动。

sentences.en: If your partner, I don't know, goes off on a rant about how awful their boss is or how shitty one of their friends is, show how much you care by listening instead of, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你的伴侣，我不知道，开始抱怨他们的老板有多糟糕或者某个朋友有多混蛋，通过倾听而不是……来表达你的关心，你知道的，

sentences.en: listing off tips to deal with the situation or offering to do something that they might not even need you to do.
sentences.zh: 列出一堆应对当前状况的建议，或者主动提出去做一些对方甚至根本不需要你做的事。

sentences.en: They may want empathy and just validation more than anything else and probably involves
sentences.zh: 他们可能最需要的是感同身受和认同，而这往往需要你付出

sentences.en: a lot less from you financially, personally, in terms of your time and a lot of other limited resources.
sentences.zh: 极少的财务、精力和时间成本，以及其他很多有限的资源。

sentences.en: I hope you enjoyed this more bite-sized episode.
sentences.zh: 希望你们喜欢这期比较短小精悍的节目。

sentences.en: I'm trying to get into the habit of kind of varying how long the episodes are, like shorter, longer.
sentences.zh: 我正试着养成一种习惯，让节目的时长有所变化，有长有短。

sentences.en: That's literally what I just said.
sentences.zh: 这不就是我刚刚说的话吗。

sentences.en: But you get my gist, just so that there's a bit of variety and you don't have to sit back and listen to some 50 minute ramble about things you might not even care about.
sentences.zh: 但你懂我的意思，就是为了有点变化，让你不用坐着听一听就是50分钟关于你可能根本不感兴趣的事情的闲聊。

sentences.en: Get to the point, Gemma, I understand.
sentences.zh: 直接说重点吧，杰玛，我懂的。

sentences.en: Um, next week we're going to talk about love languages.
sentences.zh: 嗯，下周我们要聊聊爱的语言。

sentences.en: I have been discussing this with my friends for years and I kind of started to think whether they're valid, whether they're actually a reliable tool for assessing what you need in
sentences.zh: 我和朋友们讨论这个话题已经好多年了，我开始思考它们是否真的有用，它们是否确实是评估你在

sentences.en: a relationship.
sentences.zh: 亲密关系中需求的一种可靠工具。

sentences.en: We're doing a lot of relationship-based podcasts at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我们最近做了很多关于亲密关系的播客。

sentences.en: I also just realized that recently as well.
sentences.zh: 我最近也刚刚意识到这一点。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I'm just really into the social psychology at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我最近就是对社会心理学很感兴趣。

sentences.en: It's just really, uh, quite tantalizing and very interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很，呃，相当吸引人，也非常有趣。

sentences.en: Um, hence why you're seeing a lot more of those people-focused episodes on your feed.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以你会发现你的订阅源里多了很多这类以人际为中心的节目。

sentences.en: If you don't like it, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 如果你不喜欢，也没关系。

sentences.en: More of the positivism and more of the biological psychology is coming back soon.
sentences.zh: 更多积极心理学和生物心理学的内容很快就会回归。

sentences.en: But this is a podcast about your 20s and the relationships we form in our 20s are, I think, probably one of the most important aspects.
sentences.zh: 但这是一档关于你二十岁人生的播客，而我们在二十岁时建立的人际关系，我认为，可能是最重要的方面之一。

sentences.en: Um, also I say this every episode, but if you have made it this far, please, um, if you feel inclined, if you have a few extra five seconds, really five seconds, 10 seconds, um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我每期节目都会说，如果你听到了这里，请，嗯，如果你愿意的话，如果你有多余的五秒钟，真的只要五秒钟、十秒钟，嗯，

sentences.en: leave the podcast or review on either Spotify or Apple podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在Spotify或Apple Podcasts上给播客留个评价吧。

sentences.en: But if you don't want to do it, if you think that that's going to reinforce any people-pleasing tendencies, don't do it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不想做，如果你觉得这会助长任何讨好型人格的倾向，那就别做。

sentences.en: You know, set those boundaries.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，设立好这些界限。

sentences.en: You don't owe me anything, um, but it would be very nice.
sentences.zh: 你并不欠我什么，嗯，不过要是能做的话我会非常感激。

sentences.en: Um, and thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢你们的收听。

sentences.en: Thanks for supporting the podcast as always.
sentences.zh: 一如既往地感谢大家对播客的支持。

sentences.en: Drop a line in, um, on the website or on Instagram if you have any ideas that you really want me to kind of look into.
sentences.zh: 如果你有什么特别想让我研究的想法，可以在，嗯，网站上或Instagram上给我留言。

sentences.en: I love doing the research kind of more than I like recording in the episodes at the moment.
sentences.zh: 比起录制节目，我现在其实更喜欢做研究。

sentences.en: I've got all of these, like, amazing papers saved in my browser, um, that I'm just trying to get through to make these kind of as evidence-based as they have typically been.
sentences.zh: 我的浏览器里保存了所有这些，呃，非常棒的论文，我正试图把它们看完，好让这些节目像以往一样做到有理有据。

sentences.en: Um, so yeah, if there's anything else you want to add to that pile, please feel free to do so and have an amazing week, weekend, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，如果还有什么你想加进那个资料堆的，请尽管告诉我，祝大家无论身处世界何地，都能度过精彩的一周或周末。

sentences.en: And thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们的收听。

sentences.en: I've been approaching my health really differently this year.
sentences.zh: 我今年对待健康的方式真的很不一样。

sentences.en: I used to be really focused on maximizing and doing more.
sentences.zh: 我过去真的很专注于追求极致和做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And now I'm just realizing that if I listen to what my body needs, I perform way better.
sentences.zh: 而现在我才意识到，如果我倾听身体的需求，我的表现反而会好得多。

sentences.en: And that's why I am obsessed with my Whoop.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么我对我的Whoop手环爱不释手。

sentences.en: Truly, you guys, you know I'm such a data and information-driven person.
sentences.zh: 真的，伙计们，你们知道我是个极其注重数据和信息的人。

sentences.en: And I love opening my Whoop app and seeing how my sleep, my stress, my strain is correlating with my mood, with my running performance, with how I'm just feeling day-to-day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢打开Whoop应用，看我的睡眠、压力、消耗是如何与我的情绪、跑步表现以及我日常的感觉相关联的。

sentences.en: I'm not an elite athlete by any means, but I do really benefit.
sentences.zh: 我绝算不上什么顶尖运动员，但我确实从中获益匪浅。

sentences.en: And I also just really enjoy knowing more about my body.
sentences.zh: 而且我也真的很喜欢能更多地了解自己的身体。

sentences.en: And Whoop also gives me these actionable, personalized insights that have made me more intentional and meant that I make smarter decisions day-to-day about what I need rather
sentences.zh: 并且Whoop还为我提供这些可操作的个性化见解，让我变得更有意识，这意味着我在日常生活中能对自己的需求做出更明智的决定

sentences.en: than just putting my foot on the gas and just going, going, going, going.
sentences.zh: 而不是一味地踩着油门拼命向前冲。

sentences.en: New members can try Whoop with a 30-day free trial before committing to a membership.
sentences.zh: 新会员可以在购买会员前免费试用 Whoop 30 天。

sentences.en: That's join.whoop.com slash psychology for your free month of Whoop.
sentences.zh: 访问 join.whoop.com 并在斜杠后输入 psychology 即可免费体验一个月的 Whoop。

sentences.en: Some people keep all their old gig tickets.
sentences.zh: 有些人保留着他们所有的旧演唱会门票。

sentences.en: It brings back the music.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回音乐。

sentences.en: It brings back the memories, even the smells.
sentences.zh: 它能唤回回忆，甚至是气味。

sentences.en: Other people collect perfume bottles or coffee mugs or overseas banknotes, classic sweaters from the 80s.
sentences.zh: 其他人则收集香水瓶、咖啡杯、海外纸币或是 80 年代的经典毛衣。

sentences.en: Collection is deeply personal.
sentences.zh: 收藏是非常私人的事情。

sentences.en: It says who we are, but it also says where we've come from.
sentences.zh: 它展现了我们是谁，但也展现了我们来自何方。

sentences.en: In the new podcast, Charmed with Sam Todd, Sam explores the memories, obsessions, and tiny treasures that become part of who we are.
sentences.zh: 在由萨姆·托德主持的新播客节目《Sam Todd 的魅力世界》中，萨姆探讨了那些成为我们生命一部分的回忆、执念和微小珍宝。
